oneLiner: Search, YouTube and a Cloud business that has become a second franchise, now being rebuilt as an AI infrastructure company that funds itself with debt and new stock. The market is betting on whether a capex program heading well past $200B a year earns a return before free cash flow is gone for good.

verdict.stance: Neutral - the cash has to show up
verdict.summary: The operating story has never been better: Cloud doubled at a 36% margin, Search queries are growing at a five-year high and the Gemini 4 models closed the cadence gap that drove the summer derating. But the third quarter showed what owning it now costs. Free cash flow went negative, buybacks have stopped, and Alphabet is issuing stock and debt while 2027 capex is set to rise significantly again. On operating EPS the probability-weighted value sits near the current price: Cloud backlog would have to convert faster than the capex grows to justify a re-rating, and a 2027 capex guide above ~$300B without matching backlog growth would push us to Cautious.
wtb: FY2027 revenue reaches ~$585B (+19%), with Cloud growing 70%+ as the $561B backlog converts (just over 55% of it within 24 months).
Operating-basis net margin holds at ~25% or better through FY2027 despite depreciation growing far faster than revenue.
Diluted shares stay at or below ~12.45B through 2027: equity issuance stops once TPU system sales and Cloud cash flow cover the build.
The market keeps paying a low-20s multiple on operating EPS (gains and losses on equity stakes excluded) at end-2027, which needs 2028 capex growth to slow.

bear.why: Revenue grows only ~10% on FY2026's ~$492B as FX, AI Mode's lower monetization and a capacity glut slow Search and Cloud at once; depreciation from a $300B+ capex year takes net margin to ~22%. With free cash flow negative and share issuance continuing, the market prices it like a utility building capacity and pays a high-teens multiple.

base.why: Cloud grows ~70% on backlog conversion and TPU system sales; Search grows high single digits as AI Overviews and AI Mode ads scale. Net margin dips to ~25.5% (from ~26.6% in Q3 2026) as depreciation outruns Cloud operating leverage. FCF returns to modestly positive late in 2027, so the multiple holds in Alphabet's historical low-20s range.

bull.why: Cloud keeps compounding near 100% as TPU systems become a merchant chip business and Search re-accelerates on query growth. Net margin expands to ~28% because Cloud margin keeps rising despite third-party capacity. Visible payback on the build earns a high-20s multiple.

scenarioModel.note: Operating basis: EPS = revenue x net margin / ~12.45B diluted shares (12.37B in Q3 2026 plus continued ATM issuance). Net margin is after-tax operating income plus net interest; gains and losses on equity securities (SpaceX, Anthropic and other stakes) are excluded because they swing EPS by dollars per quarter (+$6.26 in Q2 2026, -$0.55 in Q3). Bear 540 x 22% / 12.45 = 9.5; base 585 x 25.5% / 12.45 = 12.0; bull 630 x 28% / 12.45 = 14.2. Net cash and equity stakes add roughly $20 per share on top (Sep 30, 2026 balance sheet) and are not in the multiples. FY2026 revenue ~$492B assumes ~$135B in Q4. Siberforge estimates, not consensus; pre-print FY2027 consensus EPS was ~$15.2-15.4 (KeyCorp, Yahoo), which likely mixes in non-operating items (unverified).

debates.q: Does the capex earn a return fast enough?
debates.bull: Cloud backlog grew to $561B and Kurian says Google could serve a lot more demand with more capacity; TPU systems are sold against committed contracts, so the build is a supply response, not a bet.
debates.bear: Capex ran at ~40% of Q3 revenue and the 2026 guide implies $63-73B in Q4 alone, with 2027 set to rise significantly again. Depreciation grew 49% YoY in Q3 versus 25% revenue growth, and the margin drag compounds for years.
debates.view: This debate sets the multiple (17x vs 27x). Backlog growth per dollar of capex is the test: backlog added ~$47B in Q3 against $51B of capex. We need that ratio to hold as capex grows.

signpost.metric: 2027 capex guide vs Q4 2026 Cloud backlog
signpost.threshold: bearish if 2027 capex is guided above ~$300B while backlog grows less than $40B q/q; bullish if backlog passes $650B

debates.q: How much of the profit is cash, and who pays for the gap?
debates.bull: The weak cash-conversion flag is an accounting artifact: equity marks inflate net income but are not cash. Operating cash flow was 1.4x after-tax operating income over the trailing year, and inventory ($13.3B, up from $2.4B) is TPU systems built against signed contracts.
debates.bear: After capex, trailing FCF is $19.7B on $471B of revenue and two quarters were negative. Buybacks went from $39.8B in the first nine months of 2025 to zero in 2026, replaced by $42.9B of ATM stock sales, a $19.1B mandatory convertible and long-term debt up from $46.5B to $125.1B.
debates.view: The real issue is free cash flow, not conversion. Equity issuance turns the per-share story negative, so we model 12.45B shares and no buyback in FY2027. Persistent dilution would cut the base value more than any margin miss.

signpost.metric: Quarterly FCF and diluted share count
signpost.threshold: red flag if FCF is negative for a third straight quarter or diluted shares exceed 12.45B

debates.q: Can Search monetize AI answers at the old rate?
debates.bull: Query growth is at a five-year high including commercial queries, AI Mode queries are about 3x longer, and ads are scaling in AI Overviews and AI Mode, including multiturn ads in the US.
debates.bear: Search growth halved from +17% in Q2 to +12%, management cited lower monetization in AI Mode, and Q4 faces a couple of points of further pressure from lapping the late-2025 acceleration.
debates.view: Most of the Q3 slowdown was FX, de minimis and World Cup comparisons, not AI. A second quarter of query growth without revenue growth would show that AI answers monetize below classic search, and that caps the base case.

signpost.metric: Google Search & other growth in constant currency
signpost.threshold: below +8% in Q4 2026 while query growth is still reported as accelerating = monetization problem

thesis: Cloud is now a second franchise. It is a quarter of revenue at a margin above the group's, and the $561B backlog, just over 55% recognizable within 24 months, implies ~$155B a year of contracted revenue against a ~$123B Q3 run rate.

TPU is a merchant chip business in the making. Nearly 100 customers including Anthropic, Apple and Citadel Securities use TPUs, system sales were a meaningful Q3 growth contributor and management guides a meaningful revenue ramp in 2027; no other hyperscaler sells its own accelerators to outsiders at this scale.

The model-cadence gap closed. The Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon models are, in Pichai's words, leading at the frontier; the Gemini app reached 1B users, and first-party APIs process nearly 32B tokens a minute, more than 4x a year ago.

Legal risk has narrowed to behavioral remedies. Judge Brinkema rejected every structural ad-tech remedy on Sep 2, 2026, and the search remedies (data sharing, one-year default-deal caps, no Chrome sale) are behavioral unless the D.C. Circuit sides with the DOJ cross-appeal.
risks: Capex intensity with no ceiling yet. Trailing capex is ~34% of revenue (11% in 2022) and 2027 rises significantly again; depreciation and energy costs grow faster than revenue, and third-party capacity adds near-term Cloud margin headwinds.
Dilution replaced buybacks. Alphabet is now a net issuer of equity (ATM program with $27.6B still available, plus the 6.25% mandatory convertible), so per-share growth trails earnings growth.

Reported EPS is not the business. Trailing net income was ~150% of operating income because of equity-stake marks; Q2's +$99B gain became an $8.7B loss in Q3 as SpaceX shares fell, and the Anthropic stake (largest in $135B of non-marketable securities) is marked at private-round values.
Search monetization under AI. Lower monetization in AI Mode is now acknowledged by management; agentic browsers and ChatGPT attack the query funnel even as volumes grow.

The search appeal is open. The DOJ and 35 states seek a Chrome divestiture at the D.C. Circuit, with no argument date set and a decision unlikely before 2027; the ad-tech final judgment and Google's liability appeal are still pending (status unverified).
catalysts: Early Feb 2027: Q4 2026 report - first number for 2027 capex, Q4 backlog and FCF (debates 1 and 2).
Q4 2026 to 2027: TPU system sales ramp and third-party capacity usage show up in Cloud growth and margin (debate 1).
Quarterly: SpaceX share price and any Anthropic funding round re-mark the equity stakes, moving GAAP EPS but not operating EPS (debate 2).
Q4 2026 report: Search constant-currency growth against the lapping headwind (debate 3).
Late 2026 to 2027: D.C. Circuit argument in the search case (not yet scheduled); ad-tech final judgment and Fourth Circuit appeal.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30, 2026; reported Oct 28, 2026)
points: Search & other $63.4B (+12%), YouTube ads $11.2B (+9%), subscriptions/platforms/devices $14.3B (+11%), Network $7.5B (+1%).
Cloud $30.7B (+103%); Cloud operating income $11.1B, margin 36.2% vs 23.7%; backlog $561B vs $514B in Q2.
GAAP EPS $2.12 vs $2.87 a year ago and ~$3.00 consensus; an $8.7B loss on equity securities (mainly SpaceX) cut EPS by $0.55.
Operating cash flow $42.3B, capex $51.4B (vs $24.0B), free cash flow -$9.1B; no buybacks, $12.4B of new stock and $28.7B of notes issued.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Oct 28). Revenue missed slightly and EPS badly: the stock fell ~8-10% after hours. Excluding the equity-stake loss, EPS was about $2.67, still well below expectations, as R&D rose 36% and depreciation 49%. Search slowed to +12% from +17% in Q2; management blamed FX first, then APAC retail after the EU de minimis change and post-World Cup media normalization, and also cited lower monetization in AI Mode. YouTube ads slowed to +9% on brand advertising, with living-room viewing over a third of YouTube ad revenue. Cloud was the bright spot: revenue doubled with TPU system sales a meaningful contributor. Other Bets lost $2.0B and Alphabet-level AI research cost $7.7B. The quarter also included a $5.2B cash payment for the 2018 European Commission Android fine. Headcount was 204,757 (+8%).
guidanceProse: FY2026 capex guide unchanged at $195-205B. After $132.0B in the first nine months, that implies $63-73B in Q4, and CFO Anat Ashkenazi said capex will "increase significantly" in 2027, with the number due on the Q4 call. One secondary summary says 2027 capex will top $300B (unverified; not in the release or the call quotes we found). For Q4, management flagged a slightly larger FX headwind, a couple of points of Search pressure from lapping the late-2025 acceleration, a TPU system sales step-up, and near-term Cloud margin headwinds as third-party capacity that came online at the end of Q3 ramps. Funding is now external: $27.6B remains under the ATM equity program, and long-term debt reached $125.1B. The quarterly common dividend stays at $0.22.
segments: Google Services 75% of Q3 2026 revenue ($96.3B, +11%; operating income $39.2B): Search ~50%, subscriptions/platforms/devices ~11%, YouTube ads ~9%, Network ~6%.
Google Cloud 24% ($30.7B): GCP AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions, Workspace, and TPU system sales (product revenue).
Other Bets under 1% ($0.4B revenue, -$2.0B operating loss; mainly Waymo). Alphabet-level costs (shared AI research) are not allocated.

Investments: $135.2B of non-marketable securities (mostly Anthropic) and listed stakes including SpaceX inside $265.1B of cash and marketable securities; $34.1B of acquisitions in the first nine months of 2026 (largely Wiz, unverified).
competitive: Models: Gemini 4 competes with OpenAI and Anthropic at the frontier - Anthropic is both a rival and a large TPU customer and Alphabet holding.
Assistants and browsers: ChatGPT (~900M weekly users, unverified) and agentic browsers (Atlas, Comet) target the query funnel that Chrome and Android protect.
Cloud: AWS 28%, Azure 21%, Google 14% share (Synergy, Q1 2026, unverified), but Google is growing more than twice as fast as either.
AI silicon: TPU systems compete directly with NVIDIA for external customers, with Broadcom as design partner and, in Anthropic's case, as a channel.
moat: Search distribution at ~91% global share (unverified) through Chrome, Android and default deals, now combined with the full AI stack: own models (Gemini), own silicon (TPU), own cloud and the largest consumer AI surface. TPU makes Alphabet the one hyperscaler that is less dependent on NVIDIA pricing and can sell that advantage to others. The moat is intact; the open question is the capital needed to defend it.

valPresets.note: Valuation basis is forward earnings: TTM FCF ($19.7B through Q3 2026) is crushed by the capex program and TTM GAAP earnings are inflated by equity-stake marks ($126.8B of net securities gains in the first nine months of 2026), so forward operating EPS is the cleanest anchor.

changelog.change: Rebuilt as a v3 decision note after the Q3 2026 print: Cloud +103%, backlog $561B, but FCF -$9.1B, no buybacks, equity and debt issuance, and 2027 capex to rise significantly. Scenarios on FY2027 operating EPS excluding stake marks (bear $162 / base $276 / bull $383). Stance set to Neutral; the model-cadence worry is resolved and replaced by cash flow and dilution.
